text:
Maya: Quick sync — AtlasCorp wants a pilot: tenant isolation, customer-managed KMS, and aggressive tail latency asks. Need cross-team agreement on what we can commit.
Priya: Do they require HSM from day one? Sales said "preferred" not mandatory.
Maya: Exact ask from the brief: "dedicated pool, per-tenant keys via customer KMS, p95 <= 180ms for 2k-token text-gen on pilot traffic; HSM onboarding later."
Alex: Infra: we can provision a dedicated GPU shard and wire a KMS connector. HSM integration (attestation + rotation) is a separate vendor track ~3w. Network peering and audit-log routing are blockers.
Jordan: Security: pilot with customer-managed KMS OK, but we must avoid stating HSM-equivalent guarantees. We'll need audit export and a SOC2-aligned evidence bundle for the pilot.
Sam: Runtime: p95 180ms at 2k tokens is tight. Options: smaller model family for pilot, aggressive quantization, and warmed KV cache. Need perf runs — ~7 business days for an initial matrix.
Lee: Product proposal: Pilot MVP = customer KMS, dedicated capacity, soft SLA (p95), telemetry + regression evals, clear migration plan to HSM/hard SLA. Acceptance criteria must be measurable.
Priya: Customer timeline: wants pilot in 6 weeks. If we parallelize work across teams and flag HSM as post-pilot, it's plausible.
Maya: Agree. Action owners: Maya -> coordinate legal wording around KMS claims; Alex -> infra runbook + tickets; Sam -> runtime perf matrix; Jordan -> compliance gap doc; Lee -> eval harness; Priya -> customer SOW.
Alex: Infra checklist I'll draft: VPC peering, dedicated pool, KMS connector, audit-log pipeline, IAM scoping. ETA: 8 business days.
Sam: Runtime checklist:
```
- baseline latency (512/1024/2048)
- quant configs A/B
- batch sizing and timeouts
- KV cache warmup script
- p95/p99 under pilot-shaped load
```
Jordan: I'll produce the compliance gap and what we can promise in writing. Legal needs to review any key custody language. ETA: next Tue.
Priya: I'll negotiate with AtlasCorp to accept customer-managed KMS + soft SLA and a commitment to evaluate HSM after pilot. I'll ask for a small capacity deposit.
Lee: I'll prep an eval suite focused on hallucination and response time regressions. Link to eval template: https://redwood.internal/evals/atlas (internal).
Maya: Risks: 1) quality regressions after quant; 2) HSM delays affecting contract milestones; 3) p95 slipping under concurrency. Mitigations: evals, model fallback, clear customer comms.
deploy-bot: Ticket created: PROD-9450 "AtlasCorp pilot preflight" assigned to Alex.
Sam: If initial perf runs fail, fallback plan: propose pilot on a slightly smaller model with a documented migration path.
Maya: Good. I'll post a short acceptance criteria doc by EOD Friday and schedule a weekly checkpoint.
Priya: I'll send the draft SOW to Sales + Legal for sign-off today.
Alex: Dropping runbook link in thread when ready.
Maya: Thanks everyone — keeping pilot scoped narrowly should keep delivery timelines tight. Weekly sync same time next Wed.
